declarations.paragraph: Reporting model scores without the majority/mean baseline beside them.
Compare every candidate to an explicit baseline under the same split and metric.
Keep the baseline in every comparison table.
Complex models often lose to sane defaults once leakage is removed.
Random splits on heavily batched extracts.
Identify batch/day/file keys; forbid cross-split sharing.
Same-batch twins in train and test inflate scores.
session.calibration(...) reports calibration diagnostics on held-out data; it does not recalibrate the model.
Calibrate on validation; re-check after major retrains.
Bad calibration breaks threshold policies and capacity planning.
Pearson on arbitrary category codes.
Categorical-target links need association measures (MI, chi-square), not Pearson on codes.
Integer codes are not quantities; association ≠ ordered correlation.
Encode categoricals properly before linear models.
Treating label codes as numeric invents fake linear structure.
Shipping feature importances as 'drivers' to executives without causal language.
Separate prediction KPIs from intervention KPIs in the project brief.
Acting on correlations as causes is how ML creates policy mistakes.
Majority baselines beat careless models on accuracy.
Reading feature importance as causal effect.
A strong association can be a confounder story, not a lever you can push.
EDA association ≠ causal effect. Subgroup checks reveal Simpson-like reversals.
Name confounders; separate prediction from intervention questions.
Shipping a correlated proxy as if it were a cause harms decisions.
Reading a confusion matrix at 0.5 when you will deploy another cut.
The confusion matrix counts TP/FP/FN/TN at a chosen threshold - the anatomy of errors.
session.evaluate(...) exposes confusion diagnostics for classifiers.
Inspect errors at the operating threshold you will ship.
Single scalar metrics hide which mistakes you make.
Use a correlation threshold to identify pairs for review, then compare feature choices on validation data.
Near-duplicate columns destabilise linear coefficients.
Fixing inconsistencies using test labels.
Encode your real multi-column rules; quarantine or fix violators.
Inconsistent rows can distort both training and metrics.
Set cv folds; use nested_cv_score when selecting models/hyperparameters.
Single holdouts are noisy; nested CV separates model selection from evaluation.
Keeping test data out of model selection reduces optimism in the final performance estimate.
Assuming IID forever because training CV looked fine.
Define reference vs analysis windows; set monitoring alerts on key features.
Silent drift makes yesterday's metrics lie about tomorrow.
Parsing with dayfirst ambiguity; mixing naive and aware timestamps.
Set timestamp column and timezone policy; assign role 'time'.
Lexical 'dates' make leakage checks and rolling features wrong.
Keeping both raw and fully determined derived totals.
Derived columns that restate others add width without new information - and inflate VIF.
Use correlation pairs + VIF + domain lineage to spot re-expressions.
Ignore or drop redundant re-expressions; keep the best-measured version.
Redundant features waste regularisation budget and confuse importance.
Equating 'no finding' with 'no risk'.
Record which findings you accept/reject and why.
Over-trusting screens creates false confidence.
Tune n_components / method; decide whether to drop input columns.
Wide, collinear matrices hurt linear models; PCA is one remedy among selection/regularisation.
Reuse of test for patience checks.
Always point early stopping at validation, never test.
Stopped-on-test models overstate generalisation.
Reading average effect shapes under strong interactions as universal laws.
Plot shapes for top features stakeholders will challenge.
Direction and non-linearity matter for trust and debugging.
Set sizes; keep test frozen until the final card.
Once test results influence model choices, that test set no longer provides an independent final evaluation.
Choose partition; do not treat importance as causality.
Stakeholders will ask 'why'; answer with model attributions + caveats.
Choose standard vs minmax; exclude one-hots if you do not want them scaled.
Unscaled ranges let large-unit features dominate penalties and distances.
Set k/threshold; prefer model-based selection inside nested CV when high stakes.
Full-frame selection leaks test structure into the feature set.
Stratifying labels while still leaking groups across folds.
Set the group key; ensure no entity appears in both train and test.
Entity leakage inflates scores and fails on new entities.
Unmonitored models decay silently.
Choose candidate pairs from domain knowledge; validate in CV.
Dropping low-MI features can delete the partner of an interaction.
Fan-out duplicates overweight entities; failed matches create MNAR-looking gaps.
Remove post-outcome features; keep transform fit order after split.
Leakage is the most common way to fool yourself with tabular ML.
Reading a single end-point score as capacity diagnosis.
session.learning_curve(estimator) varies training size under CV.
Compare a weak and a strong model family's curves.
Collecting more data is expensive - curves tell you if it pays.
Set the primary metric to match business cost; ignore vanity metrics.
Leaderboards without a decision metric produce pretty but useless winners.
Do not discard features solely because Pearson is near zero.
Choosing only Pearson misses curved signal; choosing only MI misses signed linear redundancy.
Use session.compare_models on validation data, or grid_search and nested_cv_score with an appropriate cross-validation strategy.
Fix primary metric; prefer validation/nested designs for selection.
Unprincipled search overfits the selection procedure itself.
Reporting only overall accuracy for multiclass.
With more than two classes, 'average' metrics hide per-class failures unless you specify micro/macro/weighted.
Declare averaging and inspect per-class recalls before shipping.
Pick micro/macro/weighted deliberately; monitor worst class.
Macro-averages punish ignoring rare classes; micro can hide them.
Mining all slices then reporting the best as confirmatory.
Look at enough slices and something will look significant by chance.
Pre-register primary metrics; treat other slices as exploratory.
Pre-declare primary metric and primary segment.
P-hacking via dashboard clicking invents false readiness.
Tune k / method; always select inside training folds.
Catches non-linear dependence that correlation misses.
Exploding lists without re-aggregating to the modeling grain.
Flatten nested fields with a documented aggregation grain.
Feeding raw JSON strings teaches token noise, not structure.
Reporting inner-CV best scores as final performance.
When you tune, you need an outer score that never saw the tuning choices.
session.nested_cv_score separates inner selection from outer evaluation.
Set param grids narrowly; escalate compute only when needed.
Tuning on the same CV you report optimistically biases the metric.
Binning using target-aware edges on the full frame.
When effect shapes bend, binning or non-linear models beat forcing a straight line.
session.bin(...) is train-fitted. Edges chosen on test are leakage.
Tune n_bins / strategy; prefer model non-linearity when possible.
Linear coefficients hide thresholds and U-shapes.
Choose detect vs cap vs drop per column with domain owners.
Blind dropping can erase the minority class you want to detect.
Growing model complexity to chase a single holdout.
Constrain capacity; use nested CV when searching.
The demo metric that only works on train is a liability.
Order matters: split -> impute -> encode -> scale -> select -> model.
Insert select_features / handle_outliers where your recipe needs them - still after split.
Wrong order leaks or invents impossible states.
Choose keep / deliberate binning; never silent jitter without documenting.
Models can learn rounding artifacts as if they were causal thresholds.
Boasting ROC-AUC at 0.5% prevalence without PR.
ROC and PR curves show ranking quality across thresholds; PR is often kinder to reality under imbalance.
Prefer PR when positives are rare; ROC can look optimistic.
Choose ROC vs PR from prevalence and costs.
Threshold-free ranking metrics still must match the decision.
Resetting seeds until the metric looks good.
If you cannot rerun it, you cannot trust it. Seeds, package versions, and data pins matter.
Pass random_state through split/encode/search; checkpoint sessions; record BuildML/engine versions from the sheet kicker.
Fix seeds; pin data snapshot ids; log package versions.
Irreproducible wins are not wins.
Residuals show where the model systematically fails - not just how wrong on average.
For regression, plot residual vs predicted and vs key features; check heteroscedasticity.
Investigate structured residual patterns before adding complexity.
Good RMSE can hide large structured mistakes in a segment.
Claiming 0.01 AUC gains on 40 positives.
Small n makes every metric noisy. Fancy models do not create information.
With rare positives, effective sample size is the minority count, not n.
Compute minority class counts; set minimums before complex search.
Underpowered comparisons crown lucky winners.
Calling every change 'drift' without a type.
Compare feature dists vs label rates vs calibration.
Map monitoring signals to shift type and playbooks.
Retraining on more data does not fix concept drift if the world rewrote the rules.
Pick skewed columns; prefer monotone transforms; validate on train folds.
Tail leverage warps linear models and some scalers.
Only reporting the global mean metric.
Overall metrics can look fine while one segment fails. Slice evaluation is mandatory for trust.
session.error_slices(...) and fairness evaluations quantify segment gaps.
Pre-declare critical slices (region, channel, cohort).
Hidden segment failure is how models harm people and businesses.
One-hotting high-card columns on small n.
When features approach or exceed rows, models memorise noise unless constrained.
Watch rows-per-feature, one-hot width, and regularisation / selection.
Cap one-hot width; select/regularise; prefer simpler models when n is small.
Over-wide matrices overfit and make holdout scores fragile.
Stratifying on a rare category until the split becomes infeasible.
session.split(stratify=True) stratifies on the target when classification.
Stratify on target; only add secondary strata if levels are thick enough.
Unstratified tiny positives make metrics lottery tickets.
Transforming y without inverting for reporting.
Know the shape of y: class mix for classification, centre/spread/tails for regression.
Target screens in EDA summarise y; modeling choices should cite them.
For regression, consider log-target only with domain justification.
Metrics and transforms depend on y's shape.
When rows are ordered in time, random splits let the future train the past.
Set the time column and cutpoints; consider gap between train and test.
Random splits can place later observations in training and earlier observations in evaluation, which may not represent the intended forecasting task.
session.tune_threshold(...) searches operating points on a validation partition.
Set costs / capacity constraints; tune on validation, freeze for test.
0.5 is rarely the right cut.
Using label-time calendar fields as predictors.
Calendar parts and lags are features only if they would be known at prediction time.
session.extract_dates builds calendar fields; lags need careful as-of joins.
Only extract parts known at score time; build lags with as-of discipline.
Future-looking time features are classic leakage.
Re-implementing preprocessing by hand in the serve path.
Point artifacts at your registry; pin versions; test parity on a golden batch.
Train-serve skew is a top cause of 'it worked in the notebook' failures.
Showing +/-sigma from training residuals as if it were predictive uncertainty.
A point prediction without uncertainty invites overconfident decisions.
Use probabilistic models / calibration / quantile approaches when stakes require intervals. session.learn('probabilistic-uncertainty') introduces the vocabulary.
Choose interval method matching stake level.
Capacity planning needs ranges, not bravado.
Swap the column you inspect; compare several features before modeling.
Shape drives transforms, outlier policy, and model family choice.
Pick threshold; drop/ignore one column at a time; recompute VIF.
Interpretation collapses under collinearity; trees care less.

paragraphs: Before you open a notebook, write the decision the model is supposed to support. A prediction without a decision is a report, not a product.
Plain version: say who will use the score, when they see it, and what they will do differently if the score is high versus low.
Problem framing fixes the prediction target, the decision horizon, the action space, and the cost of errors. EDA numbers only become evidence after those choices are explicit.
BuildML treats framing as a teaching and readiness concern: diagnostics can describe the frame, but they cannot invent the business decision.
The same CSV supports many incompatible tasks; framing picks one.
Metrics, splits, and leakage rules all depend on when the outcome is known.
After running the demonstration, replace the synthetic frame with your dataset and update the roles.
Rewrite the decision comment: user, action, horizon, and cost of mistakes.
If unsupervised, omit target and use session.learn('cluster-validity-not-truth') instead.
Starting EDA before writing the decision the score will change.
Treating 'predict churn' as framing when the real question is 'whom to call this week'.
Changing the target definition after model selection without restarting validation.
Write the decision, horizon, and action space in plain language.
Name the label column and when it becomes known relative to prediction time.
List which error is worse (false positive vs false negative, or over- vs under-prediction).
